documents.none: No document open. Generate or open an asset to get started.
documents.noProjectBody: A document is a file inside a project. Open one, or make one, to begin.
documents.importProjectBody: The files will be copied into the selected project, then opened in the studio.
documents.missing: This document is no longer open.
documents.saveRefusedGuiTooNew: This interface comes from a file written by a newer build of the studio. Saving would erase what this build cannot read — update the studio, or start from a new interface.
documents.saveRefusedGuiUnreadable: This interface could not be read: the file is incomplete or damaged. Saving would write a blank screen over it — repair the file, or start from a new interface.
documents.guiTooNew: This interface was written by a newer build of the studio. It opens empty and saving is refused.
documents.guiUnreadable: This interface could not be read. It opens empty and saving is refused, so the file is not overwritten.
documents.guiEmpty: This interface is empty. The next lot lays its components down.
documents.saveRefusedIncomplete: This edit opened without the clips whose media are missing. Saving would erase them from the file — import the media into the project, then open the edit again.
documents.saveRefusedMontageHoldsMore: This edit comes from an OpenTimelineIO file holding more than the studio composes — a marker, an effect, a transition. The edit is written back whole, so saving would erase those parts. Use the edit’s own export, in the File menu, or start from a new edit.
documents.montageHoldsMore: This edit holds parts the studio cannot write back — {{parts}}. It opens read-only: saving is refused while they are there.
documents.importLoses: An edit from another application brings the standard part alone. What the studio does not rebuild — {{parts}} — starts from its default.
documents.saveRefusedSkyHoldsMore: This sky comes from a glTF file holding more than the studio composes — a second scene, another light, an extension of its own. Only the sun and the horizon are written back, so saving would erase the rest. Use File ▸ Export ▸ Sky, or start from a new sky.
documents.skyHoldsMore: This sky holds parts the studio cannot write back — {{parts}}. It opens read-only: saving is refused while they are there.
documents.saveRefusedSceneHoldsMore: This scene comes from a glTF file holding meshes or animations the studio does not compose. A glTF is linked by index, so saving would erase those parts. Use File ▸ Export ▸ Scene, or start from a new scene.
documents.sceneHoldsMore: This scene holds parts the studio cannot write back — {{parts}}. It opens read-only: saving is refused while they are there.
documents.saveRefusedMaterialHoldsMore: This material comes from a MaterialX file holding more than one. The studio writes only one back: saving would erase the rest. Use File ▸ Export ▸ Material, or start from a new material.
documents.materialHoldsMore: This material holds parts the studio cannot write back — {{parts}}. It opens read-only: saving is refused while they are there.
documents.unlinkedClips_one: {{count, number}} clip did not find its media in this project and was not opened — {{files}}
documents.unlinkedClips_many: {{count, number}} clips did not find their media in this project and were not opened — {{files}}
documents.unlinkedClips_other: {{count, number}} clips did not find their media in this project and were not opened — {{files}}
documents.hiddenTabsHint: Opens the list of tabs the strip has run out of room for
documents.hiddenTabHint: Goes to this document and brings its tab back into the strip
documents.saveBody: If you do not save them, they will be lost.
documents.deleteBody: The file is removed from the project folder. This cannot be undone.
documents.overwriteBody: Another application has written to this file since the studio read it. Saving now replaces those changes, and they will be lost.
documents.flattenTitle: Flatten the image of “{{title}}” into its {{format}}?
documents.flattenBody: A {{format}} carries no {{lost}}. The file receives the image as you see it and takes that format’s extension; the studio document keeps your layers intact. This will not be asked again for this document.
documents.closeHint: Takes the tab off the bar; the document stays in the project
documents.closeOthersHint: Closes every other tab, one after another
documents.renameHint: Changes the document’s name everywhere it is written — its file included
documents.deleteHint: Removes the document from the project, its file included

project.occupiedTitle: Set up the project “{{folder}}” in this folder?
project.occupiedBody: This folder already holds files, and it will BECOME the project: the studio adds its “assets” and “documents” folders inside it. Nothing already there is changed or moved.
project.openHint: Opens a project folder already made, with what it holds
project.switchHint: Open another project from this machine, or create one
project.useHint: Closes the open project and opens this one in its place
project.createHint: Pick a folder on disk: everything the studio produces is written there
project.leaveRunningTitle: Leave this project while generations are running?
project.leaveRunningBody: Generations running: {{count, number}}. They carry on, and what they produce is filed in this project — you will find it there when you open it again. Nothing of it lands anywhere else in the meantime.
project.closeHint: Closes every tab and hands the studio back to the home. The folder stays where it is, and the project on the shelf
project.contextHint: Open the panel where what this project is about is written
